text:
maya: quick pulse check — brought up mt-bert-v2 as a reranker candidate and ran a few quantized configs, results look...weird?
raj: weird how? numbers or perf regressions on tail queries?
maya: mostly ndcg@10/ndcg@5 drops on long-tail queries. global ndcg delta vs fp16 baseline: -0.6% for int8 dynamic, -0.2% for int8 static. mrr stable.
toni: do you have the eval command/config you used? want to reproduce locally.
maya: pasted the run below:
```bash
python eval_rerank.py --model mt-bert-v2 --weights quantized/int8_static.pt --dataset prod_holdout_2025 --split eval --metric ndcg@10,mrr --batch 256 --seed 42
```
ev an: (typo) evan: quick q — is prod_holdout_2025 the same preprocessing as offline benchmark? tokenization/sequence length?
maya: yes same tokenizer, but I changed doc truncation from 512->256 to speed up eval. could that matter?
raj: absolutely. shorter docs can remove signal for long docs -> ndcg drop on long-tail. we should keep truncation consistent with baseline.
toni: also check reranker scoring ties. quantization can introduce tiny float perturbations that change ranking of near-equal scores. that will affect ndcg but not necessarily MRR.
ev an: good point. do we have a script to compute how many queries had tie swaps?
maya: not yet. i'll run a diff on top-K lists.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: CI run 2027-03-01T10:04 completed — artifacts at s3://redwood-evals/1812345678/
maya: ran the consistent-truncation eval (512) and re-ran static int8: ndcg@10 delta improved to -0.18%. int8 dynamic still -0.45%.
raj: still not great but better. what's the absolute ndcg numbers? relative deltas are noisy for high baseline.
maya: baseline fp16 ndcg@10=0.3824, int8_static=0.3817, int8_dynamic=0.3806. mrr baseline 0.271 -> int8_static 0.2711 -> int8_dynamic 0.2708.
toni: those abs diffs are like 0.0007 and 0.0018 — need significance testing. bootstrap CI?
ev an: i'll run 1k bootstrap samples overnight and post p-values. also let's split by query length buckets and by doc length.
maya: added stratified eval: short/med/long queries. long-query ndcg drop is biggest: baseline 0.356 -> int8_static 0.349.
raj: ok that's actionable. two follow-ups: (1) rerun with KV-cache friendly quantization (per-channel) to see if we regain some rank stability, (2) sanity-check feature inputs to reranker (score normalizers) — quantization could change distribution.
toni: add an eval that measures rank-consistency: percent of queries where top-1 changed and p@1 delta. keep it lightweight.
ev an: will schedule bootstrap + bucketed evals, and also run per-channel quantization profile. ETA EOD PST.
maya: thanks — also noting dataset sampling: we used a single prod_holdout slice, may want to validate on two different weeks to avoid temporal bias.
raj: yes, please add week-over-week holdouts and the offline benchmark. if both show the same pattern, it's a real regression; if not, it's sampling noise.
maya: will update artifacts and post results in thread when ready. thanks all :thumbsup:
ops-bot: storage-bot: uploaded eval CSVs to s3://redwood-evals/1812345678/artifacts/ (8 files)
maya: one more thing — can we add a quick diff of quantized logits distribution? small shift might explain tie flips.
toni: good idea. simple histogram + KS test should catch distribution shifts.
ev an: noted. starting runs now.
maya: leaving notes in the run summary: changed truncation -> switched back to 512; added stratified buckets + bootstrap. will ping when CI finishes.
raj: perfect, thanks.
